rubric: Scores are 1 (poor) to 5 (favorable). They are planning judgments from the research, not measurements.

options.name: Tail area beside the spare, as-is
options.reason: The B4810 manual says not to use the pack in water and not to reuse it if it gets wet. An open tail and spare-tire area is a road-spray zone. No published dry pocket was found. The space remains the site for a sealed box (option b) or a relocated-spare well (option c).

options.name: Fabricated tail enclosure
options.reason: Meets the out-of-sight and cabin-free requirement if the field gap fits the packs plus ventilation and the yellow sticker still has rear GAWR margin after the lever-arm math. Box weight is unknown.

options.name: Relocate the spare and use its well
options.reason: Well size, mounting method, and distance behind the axle are not published. A hitch-mounted or bumper spare conflicts with the Fiat tow bar and is ruled out. A rear-wall carrier or a well forward of the axle stays open.

options.name: Between the frame rails, near the rear axle
options.reason: Best axle math if the packs sit on the axle. Inside frame width, tanks, exhaust, and the generator are unmeasured. Kelderman lists 35.400 in center-to-center on a Transit cutaway drawing; the clear gap is smaller and unpublished.

options.name: Split the packs, one forward and one aft
options.reason: Cuts the rear-axle moment versus putting both packs at the tail. Two enclosures, a longer harness, and paralleling leads. Still has to clear tanks, exhaust, and the spare.

options.name: Convert an existing exterior compartment
options.reason: A slam-latch rotocast bay is dry-er than the open underbelly and easier to service, but compartment size, location, and depth are unpublished. Using it spends storage the tow kit also needs.

options.name: Under the rear lift-bed platform
options.reason: Dry and serviceable, which is how several van builds mount lithium. It is not underbelly, it spends the rear garage, and a rear bed is still aft of the axle. Kept as a researched alternative, not the brief.

options.name: Hitch-mounted battery box
options.reason: The receiver is reserved for the flat-tow bar of the Fiat 500 Abarth.

options.name: Roof-mounted batteries
options.reason: High center of gravity, unknown roof structure, poor service access, and the brief puts the bank underbelly and out of sight.
